headline: Medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks arise from shared-bus Pipecat ingesting OpenMetadata outputs without documented provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata can emit content through APIs, events, webhooks, and MCP server, while Pipecat consumes text over shared-bus/session scope and can route it into LLM services. That creates a plausible default path where OpenMetadata output is treated as input by Pipecat. No provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata outputs are forwarded into Pipecat via webhook, MCP, or shared bus
IF Pipecat parses upstream text as instructions or tool directives without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of OpenMetadata events into Pipecat
Add a strict allowlist for message schemas before Pipecat processes them
Strip instructions and markup from OpenMetadata payloads before forwarding
Log and review all cross-agent messages for prompt-like content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and rejection rules for untrusted content

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, and memory/tribal-knowledge data, and Pipecat handles text, conversation state, and can send content to allowlisted third-party APIs. If they share a workspace or bus, sensitive metadata can flow from OpenMetadata into Pipecat and then outward. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata data classes include sensitive governance or lineage records
IF Pipecat forwards shared-bus content to external STT/LLM/TTS providers
mitigations: Keep OpenMetadata and Pipecat on separate workspaces or buses
Remove sensitive fields before handing data to Pipecat
Turn off external model providers for any sensitive session
Review Pipecat egress destinations and restrict them to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction and DLP checks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata supports multiple instances and MCP/API-driven writes; Pipecat also supports multiple instances with shared-bus shared state. If both are wired to the same mutable resource or bus, concurrent writes can collide. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so conflict risk exists in default multi-instance deployments.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared bus, file, or database
IF no external lock or transaction boundary is configured
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate namespace or topic
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
Disable one writer during bulk updates
Check for duplicate or out-of-order updates after runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control or locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata can produce lineage, governance, and trust metadata that Pipecat may ingest as text or conversation state. Pipecat then routes that content through downstream services, so an upstream mistake can be amplified if Pipecat treats it as authoritative. No verification step is documented, making a cascading error plausible.
conditions: IF Pipecat uses OpenMetadata output as an authoritative prompt or transcript
IF downstream actions or responses are generated without verification
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step before Pipecat acts
Require citations or source IDs on OpenMetadata-derived claims
Compare OpenMetadata output against a second source before use
Limit Pipecat to summarization rather than action-taking
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and rollback for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata clearly handles governance and lineage data, while Pipecat handles conversation state and can egress to third-party providers. The profiles do not specify residency, certifications, or retention mismatches, so only a documented-gap compliance concern is supportable. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not directly evidenced, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Pipecat sessions
IF the chosen Pipecat provider has stricter residency or retention rules than OpenMetadata
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through Pipecat
Check provider residency and retention settings before use
Disable analytics and telemetry for sensitive sessions
Document the data classes allowed in each agent
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows across both systems
